comment_box:
The statement that the "regulatory determination that abortion is not a “needed” service for veterans was accepted by every Secretary and Presidential administration for over 20 years." is irrelevant. Just because something has been agreed upon or enacted for 20 years does not inherently make it correct.  If anything, it means it is likely outdated and needs to be realigned with modern healthcare needs.  

The statement "Congress has consistently drawn a bright line between elective abortion and health care services that taxpayers would support" is incomplete. Whether or not a procedure is elective does not define if it is medically necessary.  The determination of if an abortion is medically necessary should be exclusively made between a patient and their healthcare team, as are all other healthcare decisions. If medical abortion is determined to be medically necessary then it should be a covered benefit, as is every other elective medical procedure that healthcare providers deem to be medically necessary at the VA. 

This plan to reinstate the full exclusion on abortions and abortion counseling from the medical benefits package to pre-2022 would also include the removal of exceptions for rape, incest, and health of the mother.  This would be backwards progress in the provision of comprehensive, fair, and necessary healthcare for female Veterans.  It is appalling and inhumane to consider that a female Veteran would not be covered or have the option to be counseled on all pregnancy options, including abortion, especially in the case of rape and incest, or for health of the mother.    

Instead of reverting policy and moving backwards, please consider instead developing a more cohesive policy that is based on modern healthcare needs, will include determinations of medical necessity with a healthcare provider, and exceptions in the case of rape and incest, or for health of the mother.
